title: Pointers through dynamic memory
summary: The path most C programmers actually need: addresses, arrays, strings, the heap, structs, and calling a function by pointer.

steps.title: Pointer declaration
steps.blurb: An address you can store and follow. Initialize it, and know who owns the object.

steps.title: Array declaration
steps.blurb: Contiguous objects. In a function parameter the array is already a pointer.

steps.title: String literals
steps.blurb: A static array with a hidden zero. Copy it before you edit it.

steps.title: Null-terminated byte strings
steps.blurb: strlen, strcmp, and memcpy assume you know where the buffer ends.

steps.title: malloc
steps.blurb: Allocated storage outlives the function and starts uninitialized.

steps.title: Struct declaration
steps.blurb: A layout of fields, with padding you do not get to interpret.

steps.title: qsort, qsort_s
steps.blurb: A function pointer is how the library calls back into your comparator.

title: Control flow without surprises
summary: Branches, loops, and the places C lets execution jump farther than the next line.

steps.title: if statement
steps.blurb: A scalar compared with zero. Brace both sides.

steps.title: for loop
steps.blurb: An index lives in the loop. Unsigned countdown is a trap.

steps.title: switch statement
steps.blurb: Cases fall through until you stop them.

steps.title: Scope
steps.blurb: A name's visibility is not the same as its lifetime.

steps.title: setjmp
steps.blurb: A non-local jump. Prefer it rarely, and mark the locals volatile.

title: Types, qualifiers, and names
summary: What the bytes mean, what const actually promises, and how to name a function pointer.

steps.title: Arithmetic types
steps.blurb: Widths are minimums unless you ask stdint.h or _BitInt.

steps.title: const type qualifier
steps.blurb: A contract on one view of an object, not a lock.

steps.title: volatile type qualifier
steps.blurb: Every access is observable. It is not a lock either.

steps.title: restrict type qualifier (since C99)
steps.blurb: A promise of no aliasing, which the compiler believes.

steps.title: Typedef declaration
steps.blurb: An alias, not a new type. Watch what const does to a hidden pointer.

steps.title: Enumerations
steps.blurb: Names for integers. C23 can fix the width.

steps.title: Union declaration
steps.blurb: One active member, ideally with a tag beside it.

title: What C23 changed in daily code
summary: The features worth using as soon as the compiler on the project actually has them.

steps.title: Predefined null pointer constant (since C23)
steps.blurb: A null pointer that is not the integer zero.

steps.title: Attribute specifier sequence (since C23)
steps.blurb: [[nodiscard]], [[fallthrough]], and the rest of the standard attributes.

steps.title: C attribute: nodiscard (since C23)
steps.blurb: Make a dropped error code a warning.

steps.title: constexpr specifier (since C23)
steps.blurb: A typed constant the compiler must fold.

steps.title: typeof operators (since C23)
steps.blurb: Name the type of an expression inside a macro.

steps.title: Arithmetic types
steps.blurb: _BitInt(N) for a width the typedefs do not offer.

steps.title: Binary resource inclusion (since C23)
steps.blurb: Include a file's bytes without a generated source file.

steps.title: ckd_add
steps.blurb: Ask whether an addition fits, instead of hoping.

title: Text and files
summary: From a literal, through formatting, to a stream you actually close.

steps.title: String literals
steps.blurb: Where the characters come from.

steps.title: strlen, strnlen_s
steps.blurb: A count of bytes before the zero, not a capacity.

steps.title: strcpy, strcpy_s
steps.blurb: A copy that trusts the destination.

steps.title: printf, fprintf, sprintf, snprintf, printf_s, fprintf_s, sprintf_s, snprintf_s
steps.blurb: A format string that must match the arguments.

steps.title: fopen, fopen_s
steps.blurb: A FILE you check, and a close you do not skip.

steps.title: errno
steps.blurb: Read it only after a call has already failed.
